title: 1 Kings 7: Solomon's House and the Brass Work of the Temple
body:
Read the chapter → [1 Kings 7](/bible/1-kings/7)

**[1 Kings 7:1-8](/bible/1-kings/7#v1)**
> <sup>[1](/bible/1-kings/7#v1)</sup> But Solomon was building his own house thirteen years, and he finished all his house.
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/1-kings/7#v2)</sup> He built also the house of the forest of Lebanon; the length thereof was an hundred cubits, and the breadth thereof fifty cubits, and the height thereof thirty cubits, upon four rows of cedar pillars, with cedar beams upon the pillars.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/1-kings/7#v3)</sup> And it was covered with cedar above upon the beams, that lay on forty five pillars, fifteen in a row.
>
> <sup>[4](/bible/1-kings/7#v4)</sup> And there were windows in three rows, and light was against light in three ranks.
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/1-kings/7#v5)</sup> And all the doors and posts were square, with the windows: and light was against light in three ranks.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/1-kings/7#v6)</sup> And he made a porch of pillars; the length thereof was fifty cubits, and the breadth thereof thirty cubits: and the porch was before them: and the other pillars and the thick beam were before them.
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/1-kings/7#v7)</sup> Then he made a porch for the throne where he might judge, even the porch of judgment: and it was covered with cedar from one side of the floor to the other.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/1-kings/7#v8)</sup> And his house where he dwelt had another court within the porch, which was of the like work. Solomon made also an house for Pharaoh’s daughter, whom he had taken to wife, like unto this porch.

- Solomon is thirteen years building his own house and finishes all his houses, including the house of the forest of Lebanon, a hundred cubits long, fifty broad, and thirty high, upon four rows of cedar pillars with cedar beams, with windows in three rows, light against light. He makes a porch of pillars, and a porch for the throne, the porch of judgment, covered with cedar from floor to floor.
- Solomon's throne sat back off a porch of judgment, an area before which men would stand while the throne rose behind and above them under its own covering. He also makes a house for Pharaoh's daughter whom he had taken to wife, a marriage made, as marriages were in that time, for political gain and standing among the nations.

**[1 Kings 7:9-12](/bible/1-kings/7#v9)**
> <sup>[9](/bible/1-kings/7#v9)</sup> All these were of costly stones, according to the measures of hewed stones, sawed with saws, within and without, even from the foundation unto the coping, and so on the outside toward the great court.
>
> <sup>[10](/bible/1-kings/7#v10)</sup> And the foundation was of costly stones, even great stones, stones of ten cubits, and stones of eight cubits.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/1-kings/7#v11)</sup> And above were costly stones, after the measures of hewed stones, and cedars.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/1-kings/7#v12)</sup> And the great court round about was with three rows of hewed stones, and a row of cedar beams, both for the inner court of the house of the Lord, and for the porch of the house.

- All these buildings are of costly hewn stones, sawed with saws within and without, from the foundation to the coping, great stones of ten and eight cubits. The great court round about is set with three rows of hewn stone and a row of cedar beams, matching the inner court of the house of the Lord and its porch.

**[1 Kings 7:13-14](/bible/1-kings/7#v13)**
> <sup>[13](/bible/1-kings/7#v13)</sup> And king Solomon sent and fetched Hiram out of Tyre.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/1-kings/7#v14)</sup> He was a widow’s son of the tribe of Naphtali, and his father was a man of Tyre, a worker in brass: and he was filled with wisdom, and understanding, and cunning to work all works in brass. And he came to king Solomon, and wrought all his work.

- King Solomon sends and fetches Hiram out of Tyre, a widow's son of the tribe of Naphtali, whose father was a man of Tyre and a worker in brass. He was filled with wisdom, understanding, and cunning to work all works in brass.
- Here the mother is named of the tribe of Naphtali, while in Chronicles she is called of the daughters of Dan, meaning she lived in the area of Dan but was of the tribe of Naphtali. The craftsman was of Israel's lineage, sent to do the brass work of the temple.

**[1 Kings 7:15-22](/bible/1-kings/7#v15)**
> <sup>[15](/bible/1-kings/7#v15)</sup> For he cast two pillars of brass, of eighteen cubits high apiece: and a line of twelve cubits did compass either of them about.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/1-kings/7#v16)</sup> And he made two chapiters of molten brass, to set upon the tops of the pillars: the height of the one chapiter was five cubits, and the height of the other chapiter was five cubits:
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/1-kings/7#v17)</sup> And nets of checker work, and wreaths of chain work, for the chapiters which were upon the top of the pillars; seven for the one chapiter, and seven for the other chapiter.
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/1-kings/7#v18)</sup> And he made the pillars, and two rows round about upon the one network, to cover the chapiters that were upon the top, with pomegranates: and so did he for the other chapiter.
>
> <sup>[19](/bible/1-kings/7#v19)</sup> And the chapiters that were upon the top of the pillars were of lily work in the porch, four cubits.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/1-kings/7#v20)</sup> And the chapiters upon the two pillars had pomegranates also above, over against the belly which was by the network: and the pomegranates were two hundred in rows round about upon the other chapiter.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/1-kings/7#v21)</sup> And he set up the pillars in the porch of the temple: and he set up the right pillar, and called the name thereof Jachin: and he set up the left pillar, and called the name thereof Boaz.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/1-kings/7#v22)</sup> And upon the top of the pillars was lily work: so was the work of the pillars finished.

- Hiram casts two pillars of brass, each eighteen cubits high, and two chapters of molten brass of five cubits each to set upon their tops, with nets of checker work and wreaths of chain work, seven for each chapter. The chapters are the ornamented capital at the top of each pillar, the crowning molding.
- The pillars are wrought with pomegranates in two rows and lily work, and Solomon sets them up in the porch of the temple, calling the right one Jachin, which means established, and the left one Boaz, which means strength. So the work of the pillars is finished.

**[1 Kings 7:23-26](/bible/1-kings/7#v23)**
> <sup>[23](/bible/1-kings/7#v23)</sup> And he made a molten sea, ten cubits from the one brim to the other: it was round all about, and his height was five cubits: and a line of thirty cubits did compass it round about.
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/1-kings/7#v24)</sup> And under the brim of it round about there were knops compassing it, ten in a cubit, compassing the sea round about: the knops were cast in two rows, when it was cast.
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/1-kings/7#v25)</sup> It stood upon twelve oxen, three looking toward the north, and three looking toward the west, and three looking toward the south, and three looking toward the east: and the sea was set above upon them, and all their hinder parts were inward.
>
> <sup>[26](/bible/1-kings/7#v26)</sup> And it was an hand breadth thick, and the brim thereof was wrought like the brim of a cup, with flowers of lilies: it contained two thousand baths.

- Hiram makes a molten sea, ten cubits from brim to brim, round, five cubits high, with a line of thirty cubits compassing it, and knops beneath the brim in two rows cast when it was cast. This great brazen basin held water for the washings.

**[1 Kings 7:27-39](/bible/1-kings/7#v27)**
> <sup>[27](/bible/1-kings/7#v27)</sup> And he made ten bases of brass; four cubits was the length of one base, and four cubits the breadth thereof, and three cubits the height of it.
>
> <sup>[28](/bible/1-kings/7#v28)</sup> And the work of the bases was on this manner: they had borders, and the borders were between the ledges:
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/1-kings/7#v29)</sup> And on the borders that were between the ledges were lions, oxen, and cherubims: and upon the ledges there was a base above: and beneath the lions and oxen were certain additions made of thin work.
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/1-kings/7#v30)</sup> And every base had four brasen wheels, and plates of brass: and the four corners thereof had undersetters: under the laver were undersetters molten, at the side of every addition.
>
> <sup>[31](/bible/1-kings/7#v31)</sup> And the mouth of it within the chapiter and above was a cubit: but the mouth thereof was round after the work of the base, a cubit and an half: and also upon the mouth of it were gravings with their borders, foursquare, not round.
>
> <sup>[32](/bible/1-kings/7#v32)</sup> And under the borders were four wheels; and the axletrees of the wheels were joined to the base: and the height of a wheel was a cubit and half a cubit.
>
> <sup>[33](/bible/1-kings/7#v33)</sup> And the work of the wheels was like the work of a chariot wheel: their axletrees, and their naves, and their felloes, and their spokes, were all molten.
>
> <sup>[34](/bible/1-kings/7#v34)</sup> And there were four undersetters to the four corners of one base: and the undersetters were of the very base itself.
>
> <sup>[35](/bible/1-kings/7#v35)</sup> And in the top of the base was there a round compass of half a cubit high: and on the top of the base the ledges thereof and the borders thereof were of the same.
>
> <sup>[36](/bible/1-kings/7#v36)</sup> For on the plates of the ledges thereof, and on the borders thereof, he graved cherubims, lions, and palm trees, according to the proportion of every one, and additions round about.
>
> <sup>[37](/bible/1-kings/7#v37)</sup> After this manner he made the ten bases: all of them had one casting, one measure, and one size.
>
> <sup>[38](/bible/1-kings/7#v38)</sup> Then made he ten lavers of brass: one laver contained forty baths: and every laver was four cubits: and upon every one of the ten bases one laver.
>
> <sup>[39](/bible/1-kings/7#v39)</sup> And he put five bases on the right side of the house, and five on the left side of the house: and he set the sea on the right side of the house eastward over against the south.

- Hiram makes ten bases of brass, four cubits long and broad and three high, with borders of lions, oxen, and cherubims, set upon four brazen wheels like chariot wheels with axletrees, naves, fellows, and spokes all molten. Upon each base he sets a laver of brass containing forty baths, five bases on the right side of the house and five on the left, with the molten sea set on the right side eastward toward the south.

**[1 Kings 7:40-47](/bible/1-kings/7#v40)**
> <sup>[40](/bible/1-kings/7#v40)</sup> And Hiram made the lavers, and the shovels, and the basons. So Hiram made an end of doing all the work that he made king Solomon for the house of the Lord:
>
> <sup>[41](/bible/1-kings/7#v41)</sup> The two pillars, and the two bowls of the chapiters that were on the top of the two pillars; and the two networks, to cover the two bowls of the chapiters which were upon the top of the pillars;
>
> <sup>[42](/bible/1-kings/7#v42)</sup> And four hundred pomegranates for the two networks, even two rows of pomegranates for one network, to cover the two bowls of the chapiters that were upon the pillars;
>
> <sup>[43](/bible/1-kings/7#v43)</sup> And the ten bases, and ten lavers on the bases;
>
> <sup>[44](/bible/1-kings/7#v44)</sup> And one sea, and twelve oxen under the sea;
>
> <sup>[45](/bible/1-kings/7#v45)</sup> And the pots, and the shovels, and the basons: and all these vessels, which Hiram made to king Solomon for the house of the Lord, were of bright brass.
>
> <sup>[46](/bible/1-kings/7#v46)</sup> In the plain of Jordan did the king cast them, in the clay ground between Succoth and Zarthan.
>
> <sup>[47](/bible/1-kings/7#v47)</sup> And Solomon left all the vessels unweighed, because they were exceeding many: neither was the weight of the brass found out.

- Hiram makes the lavers, shovels, and basins, and finishes all the work he made for Solomon for the house of the Lord: the two pillars, the two bowls of the chapters, the two networks, four hundred pomegranates, the ten bases and their lavers, the one sea, and the twelve oxen under it. All these vessels are of bright brass, cast in the plain of Jordan in the clay ground between Succoth and Zarthan, left unweighed because they were exceeding many.
  - **[Hebrews 9:7-10](/bible/hebrews/9#v7)**
    > <sup>[7](/bible/hebrews/9#v7)</sup> But into the second went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself, and for the errors of the people:
    >
    > <sup>[8](/bible/hebrews/9#v8)</sup> The Holy Ghost this signifying, that the way into the holiest of all was not yet made manifest, while as the first tabernacle was yet standing:
    >
    > <sup>[9](/bible/hebrews/9#v9)</sup> Which was a figure for the time then present, in which were offered both gifts and sacrifices, that could not make him that did the service perfect, as pertaining to the conscience;
    >
    > <sup>[10](/bible/hebrews/9#v10)</sup> Which stood only in meats and drinks, and divers washings, and carnal ordinances, imposed on them until the time of reformation.

    Into the second tabernacle went the high priest alone once every year, not without blood, which he offered for himself and the errors of the people, the Holy Ghost signifying that the way into the holiest was not yet made manifest, standing only in meats and drinks and divers washings, carnal ordinances imposed until the time of reformation, which is the coming of Christ.

**[1 Kings 7:48-51](/bible/1-kings/7#v48)**
> <sup>[48](/bible/1-kings/7#v48)</sup> And Solomon made all the vessels that pertained unto the house of the Lord: the altar of gold, and the table of gold, whereupon the shewbread was,
>
> <sup>[49](/bible/1-kings/7#v49)</sup> And the candlesticks of pure gold, five on the right side, and five on the left, before the oracle, with the flowers, and the lamps, and the tongs of gold,
>
> <sup>[50](/bible/1-kings/7#v50)</sup> And the bowls, and the snuffers, and the basons, and the spoons, and the censers of pure gold; and the hinges of gold, both for the doors of the inner house, the most holy place, and for the doors of the house, to wit, of the temple.
>
> <sup>[51](/bible/1-kings/7#v51)</sup> So was ended all the work that king Solomon made for the house of the Lord. And Solomon brought in the things which David his father had dedicated; even the silver, and the gold, and the vessels, did he put among the treasures of the house of the Lord.

- Solomon makes all the vessels of the house of the Lord: the altar of gold, the table of gold for the showbread, the candlesticks of pure gold, five on each side, with the flowers, lamps, tongs, bowls, snuffers, basins, spoons, and censers of pure gold, and the hinges of gold for the doors. When the work is ended, Solomon brings in the things David his father had dedicated, the silver, gold, and vessels, and puts them among the treasures of the house of the Lord.
